methodology.weight: Whole-fruit examples in grams, including natural peel, shell and seeds unless noted. A source may report a range, cultivar or sample mean. Chosen examples are not species averages or record comparisons. Undocumented weights are null and excluded from arithmetic.
methodology.flavorRatings: Burrow editorial ratings from 1 to 10, interpreting descriptions of ripe fruit: 1 barely sweet/tart, 5 moderate, 10 very sweet/tart. Not Brix, sugar grams, laboratory acidity, health scores or tastiness judgments. Breadfruit is rated at the mature cooking stage, plantain ripe and cooked, and olive after curing; weights remain whole fruits before cooking or curing. Cultivar, ripeness and personal perception change flavor.
methodology.availability: Burrow editorial findability bands, 1 to 5, for fresh fruit beyond its home region: 1 local harvest/specialist growers; 2 mostly regional/seasonal; 3 specialty markets; 4 regional staple traded abroad; 5 widely traded. Not a country count, current store inventory, conservation status or price. Based on described cultivation and trade, with no implied worldwide census.
methodology.geography: Origin or cultural/cultivation association, not an exhaustive distribution. Map pins mark representative places within the stated region, not a precisely known birthplace. Ancient origins and some species boundaries remain debated.
methodology.images: Individually credited Commons photos. Stored as resized JPEGs for offline play; no botanical drawings or generated substitutes.
methodology.catalog: Fruit cards include distinct species and familiar market types or cultivar groups, such as nectarines, satsumas and golden kiwifruit; the card count is not a count of unique species.

cards.name: Pear

cards.name: Blueberry

cards.name: Persimmon

cards.name: Guava
cards.origin: Tropical Americas; exact native range debated

cards.fact: Mulberries grow on trees, while similar-looking blackberries grow on canes.

weight.note: Rounded from 3.85 g, the average fruit weight across studied black-mulberry genotypes in a 2018 paper; individual genotype means ranged from 1.79 to 5.69 g.

cards.name: Avocado
cards.texture: Creamy flesh around one large seed
cards.fact: An avocado is botanically a berry with one large seed, even though it is usually eaten in savory dishes.

weight.note: A 250 g whole-fruit example within the reported 100–1,000 g range. Includes skin and seed; cultivar sizes differ widely.

cards.name: Olive
cards.origin: Mediterranean and Near Eastern cultivation heritage

location.label: Mediterranean and Near Eastern cultivation heritage

cards.availabilityBand: Fresh: specialty markets; cured olives are widely traded
cards.flavor: Savory and tangy when cured; raw fruit is bitter
cards.texture: Firm to tender flesh around a hard stone
cards.fact: Olives are usually cured before eating to reduce their natural bitterness. Like cherries, they have a stone inside.

weight.note: The Manzanilla de Sevilla cultivar averaged 4.0 g per whole, uncured fruit in a study covering 2012–2020 harvests. Weight is before curing, unlike the flavor description.

cards.name: Plantain
cards.origin: Southeast Asian and New Guinean ancestry; staple in many tropical regions

location.label: Southeast Asian and New Guinean ancestry; staple in many tropical regions

cards.flavor: Starchy when green, sweeter when ripe and cooked
cards.texture: Firm raw flesh that softens with cooking
cards.fact: Plantains are cooking bananas. As they ripen, some of their starch changes into sugar.

weight.note: Kerala Agricultural University lists 250 g per fruit for the Big Ebanga plantain clone. A whole-fruit cultivar example; flavor ratings describe ripe cooked plantain.

cards.name: Asian Pear
cards.texture: Crunchy and very juicy, even when ripe
cards.fact: An Asian pear can look round like an apple, but it is a pear, not an apple-pear hybrid.

weight.note: The Hosui Asian pear control group averaged 241 g per fruit in an irrigation study. A cultivar and treatment sample, not a universal average.

cards.name: Sour Cherry
cards.texture: Tender, juicy flesh around a hard stone
cards.fact: Sour cherries are especially popular in pies and preserves because their tart flavor balances added sweetness.

weight.note: Rounded from the National Fruit Collection measurement of 4.70 g for the Montmorency sour-cherry cultivar. Includes the stone.

cards.sourceFile: Ripe sour cherries on a branch.jpg

cards.name: Greengage
cards.origin: Middle Eastern ancestry; European cultivation heritage

location.label: Middle Eastern ancestry; European cultivation heritage

cards.texture: Juicy, tender flesh around a stone
cards.fact: Many greengages stay green even when ripe and sweet, so a green skin does not always mean an unripe plum.

weight.note: Rounded from the National Fruit Collection measurement of 30.90 g for Belgian Greengage. A whole-fruit cultivar example.

cards.imageCreator: No machine-readable author provided. Ranveig assumed (based on copyright claims).

cards.name: Persian Lime
cards.origin: Hybrid origin uncertain; Tahiti cultivation heritage

location.label: Hybrid origin uncertain; Tahiti cultivation heritage

cards.texture: Juicy flesh under a thin green rind
cards.fact: Persian limes, also called Tahiti limes, are usually larger and less seedy than Key limes.

weight.note: UF/IFAS gives 1.9 oz (54 g) as the typical whole-fruit weight for Tahiti/Persian lime. Fruit size varies by crop and harvest.

cards.name: Golden Kiwifruit
cards.origin: Chinese ancestry; modern New Zealand breeding heritage

location.label: Chinese ancestry; modern New Zealand breeding heritage

cards.flavor: Sweet with a gentle tropical tang
cards.texture: Soft yellow flesh with tiny black seeds
cards.fact: Golden kiwifruit varieties have yellow flesh, unlike the familiar green-fleshed kiwifruit.

weight.note: Rounded from 98.3 g, the mean of 1,940 Hort16A golden kiwifruit harvested in May 1995 in New Zealand and reported in the plant patent. A cultivar sample.
